speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are an 8-month-old boy with feeding difficulties and abdominal distension. To understand what is happening inside your belly, can you tell me if you have been vomiting, and if so, does the vomit look like it contains food from earlier in the day?

speaker: Patient
text: The baby has been very fussy, feeding less than usual, and the abdomen looks distended. Crying gets worse when the belly is touched.

speaker: Doctor
text: The crying when the belly is touched suggests significant pain. Have you noticed any stool that looks like currant jelly, or any rectal bleeding? REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count; REQUEST TEST: Abdominal_Ultrasound.

speaker: Patient
text: There has not been fever, vomiting, or diarrhea like a stomach infection. The baby was born at 39 weeks without birth complications. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Intussusception and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the previous doctor suspected Intussusception, have you noticed any episodes of intermittent, severe crying followed by periods of normal behavior? REQUEST IMAGES: Abdominal_Ultrasound.

speaker: Patient
text: The baby did not seem to pass stool normally and the belly swelling has become more obvious. Feeding has clearly decreased over the past few days.
